question: Should I replace my gas furnace with a heat pump?

source.title: Thinking about a heat pump? (synthetic test article)
source.publisher: Test fixture written for this repo, illustrative numbers
quotes: a typical heat pump delivers about three units of heat for every unit of electricity it uses.
A good gas furnace turns about 90 percent of its fuel into heat.
Electricity usually costs more per unit of energy than gas, so the running cost depends on both prices where you live.
Sealing and insulating first can shrink the heat you need, and lets you buy a smaller system.

explain.caption: Gas furnace or heat pump? Here is what decides it.
Colder winters mean your home needs more heat.
A heat pump moves heat in. It doesn't burn fuel.
One unit of electricity can bring in about three of heat.
But electricity often costs more than gas, which eats into savings.
Higher gas prices make the heat pump look better.
Insulating first shrinks the heat you need at all.
Payback is the years until savings cover the extra cost.
Your turn. Try your own prices and your own winter.

tradeoffs: Lower running costs are likely where gas is expensive, but not guaranteed where electricity is.
A heat pump also cools in summer, but installation can cost more than a new furnace.
Insulating first costs money too, but can mean a smaller, cheaper system.
